newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Europe slips but tops as Morocco's trade partners.
newsitem.headline: Europe slips but tops as Morocco's trade partners.

text.p: Europe grabbed the largest share of Morocco's 1996 trade, taking 63 percent of the global turnover of 113.3 billion dirhams ($11.3 billion), according to a report by Morocco's external trade bank.
In its latest review, the Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur said the North African country's trade was little changed from 1995.
European partners were responsible for 71.8 billion dirhams worth of exchanges, down 4.2 percent from the 1995's 74.9 billion. European Union members provided the bulk of the trade, the bank said.
Other main trading partners were in Asia, which accounted for 16 percent of total trade. America notched 12 percent and Africa eight percent.
Imports from Europe fell 8.1 percent while Morocco's exports rose three percent, taking its trade deficit with the continent down to 17.04 billion dirhams from 21.78 billion.
France dominated the European continent's trade, followed by Spain, Italy and Germany, the report said. But it noted France's share had fallen for three consecutive years.

French exports to Morocco fell to 20.8 percent of the total in 1996, against 21.8 the year before and 22.6 percent in 1994. French imports dropped to 28.3 percent in 1996, against 29.6 and 31.7 percent in the two previous years, respectively.

France's main exports to Morocco in value were wheat, machinery, chemical products and medicines, while the North African country's main exports in value were household appliances, clothing, citrus fruit, vegetables, fresh tomatoes, electrical cables and fertilisers.

Figures in the report underscore the Arab Maghreb Union's (AMU) failure to make significant progress as an economic grouping, the original purpose of the bloc set up in 1989. AMU consists of Morocco, Algeria, Libya, Mauritania and Tunisia.
AMU countries provided 3.4 percent of Morocco's global imports, a 44.8-percent rise in 1996 from 1995. It made up 4.8 percent of Morocco's exports.

"The increase of out purchases from the AMU is attributable to our imports from Libya (1.2 billion dirhams against 475 million, plus 155.4 percent), notably oil, and from Tunisia (368 million dirhams against 281 million, plus 31 percent), with the rise in our provision of chemical products," said the report.
